lines.speaker: patient
lines.text: My tooth is out. What should I do first?

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: Keep biting gently on the gauze for thirty to forty-five minutes.
lines.card: Bite on the gauze for 30 to 45 minutes

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: For the first day, don't rinse, spit, or use a straw.
lines.card: No rinsing, spitting or straws today

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: And please don't smoke. It slows healing.

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: Once the numbness wears off, eat soft, cool foods.
lines.card: Soft, cool foods once numbness wears off

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: Chew on the other side, and avoid hot drinks today.

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: Brush gently, but keep away from the area today.

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: From tomorrow, rinse gently with warm salt water after meals.

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: Some soreness is normal for a few days.

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: Take only the pain relief your dentist advised, exactly as directed.
lines.card: Only the pain relief your dentist advised

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: A cold pack on your cheek helps with swelling.
lines.card: Cold pack on the cheek for swelling

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: Call us if the bleeding won't stop after pressing on gauze.

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: Or if the pain gets worse after two or three days.
lines.card: Pain getting worse after 2 to 3 days

lines.speaker: dentist
lines.text: Or if you have a fever, or swelling that keeps growing.
